normalization: relative path separators are represented with forward slashes
CRLF is converted to LF before output hashing because newline spelling is not contractual in this corpus

platform_specific_contracts: Windows read-only generated-output deletion requires clearing the write attribute; POSIX unlink semantics do not

findings.finding: A MinGW-built executable must run with the UCRT runtime directory available.
Nift subprocess output must be decoded explicitly as UTF-8 rather than through the Windows cp1252 default.
Windows blocks direct deletion of Nift's read-only generated files until the write attribute is restored.
Tracked mv/rm left stale read-only generated output and metadata on Windows because owned-artifact cleanup ignored failed removal.

result: For the tested portable behavioural corpus, normalized Linux, macOS and Windows observations were equivalent; both documented platform-specific contracts passed.
limitations: This is scoped evidence for the maintained corpus and tested GitHub-hosted runners, not a claim that Nift behaves identically on every operating system or filesystem.

Symlink privilege policy, case sensitivity, POSIX permissions, locking semantics, path-length limits and exact timestamp resolution remain platform/filesystem-specific outside this portable equality claim.
The detailed per-platform artifacts are generated by the maintained workflow; this compact record retains their run identity and archive digests.
